title: Theater schedules: four shows a day, week-long runs
summary: Theaters ran about four shows a day, five on weekends, plus an Apollo midnight show, with one-week engagements.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How many shows a day would you play in a theater?

Well, about four shows a day, we did, uh-huh. And they would run a movie, a short movie between them shows, but actually the first show would go on, oh, I -- and this is, approximately speaking, around 12:00 noon or somewhere, and the last show would go on about 11:00 at night, and this was the way those -- yeah, this was the way those theaters operated.

Of course, some days we'd do more shows. On the weekends probably we'd do five shows sometimes. And then once a week they'd a midnight show at the -- at the Apollo Theater, so this was a long show. We'd just go on until time without end on that show, and a lot of performers would come in to watch that show, you know.
Approximately How long engagements did you get? I mean a week, two weeks? How long
did you stay in a theater?
One week, never over a week. No, we never -- we never stayed over a week. No, it was just the one week engagement.

Seven days, yeah. Yeah, we never stay -- we never stayed over -- we played a week, and that was it. And, of course, the biggest portion of our work was one nighters back in those days, you know. Well, we relished the thought of doing theaters. You know, even if you were tied up all day, at least you were in one place, you know. You weren't jumping all around.
